sources.title: Country Reports on Terrorism 2003 — Egyptian Islamic Jihad (historical FTO reporting)

sources.title: Country Reports on Terrorism 2019 (EIJ historical context)

sources.title: Armed Islamic Group (GIA) — narrative summary
sources.publisher: United Nations Security Council ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee
sources.notes: UN GIA narrative: 1993 campaign of terrorist acts; GSPC formed 1998 by Hassan Hattab as splinter of GIA.

sources.title: Al-Itihaad al-Islamiya (AIAI) — narrative summary
sources.publisher: United Nations Security Council ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee
sources.notes: UN AIAI narrative: established approx. 1982-1984; sought to overthrow the government in Somalia; operated in Somalia and Ethiopia; Hassan Dahir Aweys senior leader; UN Panel describes AIAI as ideological forerunner/predecessor to Al-Shabaab.

sources.title: Letter dated 9 November 2016 from the Panel of Experts on Somalia (S/2016/919)
sources.notes: UN Panel reporting on Somalia: AIAI as ideological forerunner and personnel network within the broader Somali Islamist ecosystem.

sources.title: Letter dated 2 November 2017 from the Panel of Experts on Somalia (S/2017/924)
sources.notes: UN consolidated sanctions reporting: AIAI operated in Somalia/Ethiopia; describes AIAI elements merging into Al-Shabaab without reducing Al-Shabaab's origins to a single parent.

sources.title: Tunisian Combatant Group (TCG) — narrative summary
sources.publisher: United Nations Security Council ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee
sources.notes: UN TCG narrative: created 2000 by Seifallah ben Omar ben Mohamed ben Hassine and associates incl. Tarek al-Maaroufi; links to Al-Qaida-related camps in Afghanistan.

sources.title: Tarek ben Habib ben al-Toumi al-Maaroufi — narrative summary
sources.publisher: United Nations Security Council ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee
sources.notes: UN al-Maaroufi narrative: TCG associate with Afghanistan camp links; European network disruption context.

sources.title: Patterns of Global Terrorism 2002 — Tunisian Combatant Group (historical)
sources.notes: U.S. State historical reporting: TCG sought to establish an Islamic regime in Tunisia and targeted U.S. and Western interests.

sources.title: Moroccan Islamic Combatant Group (GICM) — narrative summary
sources.publisher: United Nations Security Council ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee
sources.notes: UN GICM narrative: emerged in the 1990s from Moroccan recruits at Al-Qaida training camps in Afghanistan; listed 2002 for association with Al-Qaida.

sources.title: Libyan Islamic Fighting Group (LIFG) — narrative summary
sources.publisher: United Nations Security Council ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee
sources.notes: UN LIFG narrative states LIFG participated with GICM in planning the May 2003 Casablanca bombings; preserved as UN sanctions narrative assessment (GICM profile only; no LIFG node created).

sources.title: Country Reports on Terrorism 2002 — Moroccan Islamic Combatant Group (historical)
sources.notes: U.S. State historical reporting: GICM described as Al-Qaida-affiliated; Moroccan extremists associated with GICM implicated in 11 March 2004 Madrid attacks.

sources.title: Country Reports on Terrorism 2007 — GICM assessment (historical)
sources.notes: U.S. State 2007 reporting: assessed GICM had disintegrated; remaining former members likely lacked capability to conduct attacks as a coherent group.

sources.title: Letter dated 16 November 2015 from the Panel of Experts on Libya (S/2015/891)
sources.notes: UN Panel S/2015/891: Al-Battar Brigade created 2012 to support ISIL in Syria/Iraq; many members returned to Libya spring 2014; ISIL Wilayat Barqa outcome of fusion between Al-Battar and IYSC/MSSI.

sources.title: Outlasting the Caliphate: The Evolution of the Islamic State Threat in Africa (CTC Sentinel)
sources.publisher: Combating Terrorism Center (CTC) at West Point
sources.notes: CTC research: Libyan fighters in Syria formed Katibat al-Battar al-Libi, aligned with ISIS after its split with Jabhat al-Nusra, later returned to Libya, contributing to the Derna militant ecosystem.

sources.title: Ansar al-Dine (Ansar Dine)
sources.notes: NCTC April 2026: formed Nov 2011 under Iyad Ag Ghali; Tuareg-origin; association with AQIM from mid-2012; seized northern Mali territory after 2012 coup context; French intervention 2013 displaced; reemerged 2016; merged March 2017 into JNIM; Iyad became JNIM emir.

sources.title: Al-Murabitun
sources.notes: NCTC April 2026: formed 2013 from merger of al-Mulathamun Battalion and another AQIM splinter (commonly MUJAO/Tawhid Wal Jihad in West Africa); Al-Qaida-aligned; one of four groups forming JNIM 2017; 2015 faction defected to ISIS (ISIS-Sahel lineage); Belmokhtar faction retained AQ alignment; operates within JNIM.

sources.title: Terrorist Groups — North and West Africa (historical)
sources.notes: NCTC historical material: al-Murabitun formed 2013 from merger of al-Mulathamun and MUJAO/Tawhid Wal Jihad faction; MUJAO operated in Sahel/Sahara within the armed Islamist landscape of northern Mali.

sources.title: ISIS-Sahel
sources.notes: NCTC ISIS-Sahel profile: lineage from the 2015 Al-Murabitun faction defection; only that faction is treated as ISIS-Sahel lineage, not the whole Al-Murabitun.
